mainTopic: The source for the four death penalties and for stoning the other נסקלין; the משנה listing the נסקלין and רבי יהודה's view on one's mother
overview: The גמרא first asks how רבי יאשיה knows that חנק exists at all, since the תורה never mentions it. רבא answers that all four death penalties are a received tradition. The גמרא then explains that רבי יונתן said 'not because it is lenient' because he holds like רבי שמעון, for whom סייף is lighter than חנק. Next, רבי זירא asks אביי which phrase links the other stoned sinners to אוב וידעוני. אביי answers that the link is ״דמיהם בם״, and the phrase ״מות יומת״ teaches something else: a murderer may be killed in any way when the written death is not possible. Later, רבינא explains that linking through ״מות יומת״ would have pointed to אשת איש and her lighter death, חנק. A new משנה then lists everyone who is stoned and discusses the double prohibitions for one's mother, father's wife and daughter-in-law. The גמרא explains that רבי יהודה's view follows רבי עקיבא, that קידושין do not take effect in a relationship forbidden by a לאו. רב אושעיא begins a challenge from a משנה about יבום, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How does רבי יאשיה know strangulation exists at all?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן's view makes sense because of רבי's reasoning, but רבי יאשיה's view seems to leave no source that חנק even exists. Perhaps the most lenient death is סייף, the sword.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works for רבי יונתן, because רבי explains his reason. But for רבי יאשיה, how do we know there is any such thing as חנק? Maybe the lightest death is the sword!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יאשיה. If the תורה never mentions strangulation, how does he know it exists?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יונתן, רבי gave a reason that points directly to חנק: a death that leaves no mark on the body. רבי יאשיה only says to choose the most lenient punishment. Without a source for חנק, maybe the most lenient one is סייף, which the תורה does mention.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for (this view). It sets up a contrast with a view that has a problem.
Strangulation, one of the four court death penalties
Sword, execution by beheading
Say instead / perhaps

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Yonatan,
it works as Rabbi explains the reason.
phrases.notes: Earlier, רבי said a death 'by Heaven' leaves no mark, so an unspecified court death must also leave no mark. That points to חנק.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yoshiya,
from where do we know there is strangulation in the world at all?
Say it is the sword!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹנָתָן כִּדְקָא מְפָרֵשׁ רַבִּי טַעְמָא אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן on an unspecified death penalty
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יאשיה's view that an unspecified death means the most lenient one, חנק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since חנק is never mentioned in the תורה, nothing shows it exists. So the most lenient punishment might be סייף.

steps.title: The four death penalties are a received tradition
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that all four death penalties are known through tradition, so the existence of חנק is not in doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the four death penalties are known to us by tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. Everyone knows from tradition that there are four death penalties, and חנק is one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was whether חנק exists at all. רבא says its existence comes from tradition and does not need a פסוק. So רבי יאשיה only has to decide which death applies to which sin. Once חנק is known to exist, it can be the lenient one.

keyTerms.meaning: The four court death penalties: stoning, burning, beheading, and strangulation
They are learned as a received tradition

steps.whatToRemember: The existence of all four death penalties, including חנק, is a tradition. The arguments in this סוגיא are only about which death applies to which sin.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The four death penalties
are learned as a tradition.
phrases.notes: Here 'גמרא' doesn't mean the Talmud. It means a teaching handed down from teacher to student.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אַרְבַּע מִיתוֹת גְּמָרָא גְּמִירִי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a source outside the פסוקים (tradition)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a פסוק, maybe חנק doesn't exist and the lightest death is סייף
steps.terutzMaskana: All four deaths are known by tradition, so חנק exists and can be the lenient choice

steps.title: What does 'not because it is lenient' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what is meant by the phrase 'לא מפני שהיא קלה' in the earlier ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'not because it is lenient' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about a phrase from the earlier ברייתא. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונתן said that an unspecified death means חנק, but not because חנק is the most lenient. The גמרא wants to know why he avoided that simple reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Not because it is the lenient one
What (does it mean)?

phrases.english: What is meant by "not because it is lenient"?
phrases.notes: This quotes רבי יונתן's words from the earlier ברייתא about an unspecified death penalty.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לֹא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִיא קַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the source for חנק to the wording of the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יונתן says his ruling is not based on חנק being the most lenient

steps.title: It depends on the רבי שמעון and רבנן dispute
steps.stepSummary: The two תנאים split along the disagreement between רבי שמעון and רבנן over which death is lightest, so רבי יונתן does not rely on leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree in the same argument as רבי שמעון and רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers. This argument follows the famous dispute between רבי שמעון and רבנן about whether חנק or סייף is the lightest death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבנן hold that חנק is the lightest death, and רבי שמעון holds that סייף is lighter. רבי יאשיה follows רבנן, so for him 'the most lenient' means חנק. רבי יונתן follows רבי שמעון, so for him חנק is not the lightest. That is why he says his ruling is 'not because it is lenient' and relies on a different source that points to חנק.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree
A dispute
The Sages (majority view)

phrases.english: They disagree in the dispute of Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: That dispute is about which death is the lightest: strangulation or the sword.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָמִיפַּלְגִי בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase shows that the תנאים follow the רבי שמעון and רבנן dispute over which death is lightest, so רבי יונתן does not rely on leniency

steps.title: Which phrase teaches stoning for the other sinners?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks אביי about the sinners who are stoned but whose stoning is not written. They learn it from אוב וידעוני, but through which phrase: 'מות יומתו' or 'דמיהם בם'?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked אביי: the other sinners who are stoned, where stoning is not written for them, learn it from אוב and ידעוני. Which phrase is the comparison built on, 'מות יומתו' or 'דמיהם בם'?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי זירא asks אביי which words in the פסוק of אוב וידעוני carry the comparison to the other stoned sinners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For several sins the תורה says only that the sinner dies, and the punishment of stoning is learned from אוב וידעוני. That פסוק has two possible linking phrases. רבי זירא wants to know which one makes the link, because each choice could teach the law to a different group of sins.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who are executed by stoning
Stoning
Types of sorcerers who claim to talk with the dead
'They shall surely be put to death'
'Their blood is upon them'

steps.whyThisMatters: The answer decides which sins are linked to stoning, since only a sin whose פסוק shares the same phrase can learn from אוב וידעוני.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Abaye:
The rest of those who are stoned
about whom stoning is not written,
since they learn it from the necromancer and sorcerer,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:27

phrases.english: through what do they learn it?
Do they learn it from "they shall be put to death,"
or do they learn it from "their blood is upon them"?
phrases.notes: Both phrases appear in the same פסוק about אוב and ידעוני, so either one could be the link.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְאַבָּיֵי שְׁאָר הַנִּסְקָלִין דְּלָא כְּתִיב בְּהוּ סְקִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the source for stoning
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the comparison to אוב וידעוני rests on 'מות יומתו' or on 'דמיהם בם'

steps.title: אביי: the link comes from the phrase 'their blood is upon them'
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers רבי זירא that the unwritten stoning cases are learned from the phrase דמיהם בם, since otherwise that repeated phrase would serve no purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: They learn it from 'their blood' and 'their blood is upon them.' For if they learned it from 'they shall surely be put to death,' why would I need the repeated 'their blood' and 'their blood'?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from the last step. He says the connection to אוב וידעוני is made through the words דמיהם בם, not through מות יומתו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof is that the תורה repeats the phrase דמיהם בם in these cases. If the link to stoning came from מות יומתו, that repeated phrase would have no job. So it must be the phrase that makes the link.

keyTerms.meaning: They learn it (by comparing two פסוקים)
Their blood is upon them
They shall surely be put to death

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is אביי answering רבי זירא's question.

phrases.english: They learn it from "their blood" and "their blood is upon them,"
for if they learned it from "they shall surely be put to death,"
why do I need "their blood" and "their blood"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בִּ״דְמֵיהֶם״ ״דְּמֵיהֶם בָּם״ גָּמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רבי זירא's question in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which phrase links the unwritten stoning cases to אוב וידעוני.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase דמיהם בם, because otherwise its repetition would be pointless.

steps.title: But then 'they shall surely be put to death' would be pointless
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns אביי's own argument around: if the link is from דמיהם, then the phrase מות יומתו would have no job.
steps.simpleTranslation: But rather, what? They learn it from 'their blood' and 'their blood'? Then why do I need 'they shall surely be put to death'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי using his own kind of reasoning. If we use דמיהם for the link, the words מות יומתו seem wasted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said a phrase must have a job, or else it's extra. The same test now hits the other phrase. Unless מות יומתו has some other job, we have the same problem on the other side.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather, what? (turning the argument around)
Why do I need it?

phrases.english: But rather, what?
They learn it from "their blood" and "their blood"?
Then why do I need "they shall surely be put to death"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי, בִּ״דְמֵיהֶם״ ״דְּמֵיהֶם״ גָּמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer by applying his reasoning to the other phrase.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the link comes from דמיהם בם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an unused phrase proves it is the source, then מות יומתו would also be unused if the link came from דמיהם.

steps.title: 'They shall surely be put to death' has its own job
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא: מות יומת teaches that if a murderer can't be killed the way written for him, he may be killed in any way possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: 'The one who struck shall surely be put to death, he is a murderer.' I would only know to kill him with the death written for him. From where do we know that if you can't kill him with the death written for him, you may kill him with any death you are able to? The verse says: 'The one who struck shall surely be put to death,' meaning in any way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the words מות יומתו are not wasted, because a ברייתא learns a different law from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from מות יומת by a רוצח that if the normal death can't be carried out, any death may be used. Since that phrase is busy teaching this, it is free to stay out of the stoning link. So אביי's answer stands: the link to stoning comes from דמיהם בם.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Murderer
I would only know
From where do we know?
The verse says (to teach this)
In any way

steps.whatToRemember: The unwritten stoning cases are linked to אוב וידעוני through דמיהם בם. The phrase מות יומת has a separate job: if you can't use the written death, you may use any death.

phrases.english: As it was taught: "The one who struck shall surely be put to death; he is a murderer" —
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:21

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בְּמִיתָה הַכְּתוּבָה בּוֹ.
phrases.english: I would only know to kill him with the death written for him.
phrases.notes: For a murderer, the death written for him is the sword, סייף.

phrases.english: From where do we know that if you are unable
to kill him with the death written for him,
that you may kill him with any death
that you are able to kill him with?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״מוֹת יוּמַת הַמַּכֶּה״ – מִכׇּל מָקוֹם.
phrases.english: The verse says: "The one who struck shall surely be put to death" — in any way.
phrases.notes: The doubled wording 'מוֹת יוּמַת' is what teaches 'in any way.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא: ״מוֹת יוּמַת הַמַּכֶּה רֹצֵחַ הוּא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7 by giving מות יומתו a separate job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the phrase is needed for a different law, so it is not extra.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מות יומתו would be extra if it weren't the source of the stoning link.
steps.terutzMaskana: מות יומתו teaches that any death may be used when the written one isn't possible, so the stoning link comes from דמיהם בם.

steps.title: רב אחא of Difti: What was the problem with learning from 'they shall surely be put to death'?
steps.stepSummary: Later, רב אחא מדפתי asks רבינא why רבי זירא saw a problem in the possibility that the link comes from מות יומתו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא of Difti said to רבינא: And if they do learn it from 'they shall surely be put to death,' what is difficult for him?
steps.whatsHappening: Later אמוראים look back at רבי זירא's question. רב אחא מדפתי asks what would be wrong if the source were מות יומתו, and this sets up the next move in the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's question suggested that learning from מות יומתו would cause some problem. רב אחא מדפתי wants to know what that problem is. The answer comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: רב אחא from the town of Difti
רבינא, a later אמורא
What is difficult for him?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:
And if they learn it from "they shall surely be put to death,"
what is difficult for him?
phrases.notes: 'Him' means רבי זירא, who asked which phrase was the source.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the resolved exchange to ask what was behind רבי זירא's original question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What difference or difficulty would result if the stoning link were learned from מות יומתו.

steps.title: Maybe the adulteress was the worry
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי suggests that רבי זירא was worried about אשת איש. Since her פסוק also says ״מות יומת״, we might link her to אוב וידעוני and wrongly give her סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the case of a married woman troubled him: we might link the words 'shall be put to death' to אוב וידעוני and say, just as there it is stoning, so too here it is stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדפתי continues his question by testing a first suggestion. He asks whether רבי זירא's worry was the case of אשת איש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about adultery also uses the words ״מות יומת״. If the link to אוב וידעוני came from those words, every ״מות יומת״ case, including אשת איש, would become סקילה. That would be a real problem, so this suggestion might explain רבי זירא's concern.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion the גמרא is about to test)
A married woman (here, one who committed adultery)
To come and learn (to derive one case from another)
Just as there ... so too here (the comparison formula)

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: If you say the case of a married woman was troubling him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי זירא. The פסוק is ויקרא 20:10.

phrases.english: that we would come and learn 'shall be put to death' from אוב and ידעוני:
just as there it is by stoning,
so too here it is by stoning?
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the married woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first candidate answer to רב אחא מדפתי's question from step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was אשת איש the case that made רבי זירא afraid of linking through ״מות יומתו״?

steps.title: A married woman cannot be stoned anyway
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected. The תורה gave סקילה specifically to an ארוסה, which shows that a נשואה is not stoned, so nobody would mistakenly learn סקילה for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Torah said a betrothed woman is stoned, we can infer that a fully married woman is not stoned.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדפתי knocks down his first suggestion. אשת איש could not have been רבי זירא's worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה gives סקילה to an ארוסה, a betrothed woman who has not yet entered marriage. If every married woman were stoned anyway, there would be no reason to single out the ארוסה. So a נשואה must get a different death, and no comparison to אוב וידעוני could change that.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One (the Torah)
A betrothed woman (after קידושין, before נישואין)
A fully married woman
By implication, we can infer

phrases.english: Since the Torah said a betrothed woman is by stoning,
it follows that a married woman is not by stoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא אֲרוּסָה בִּסְקִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the אשת איש suggestion from step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects אשת איש as the source of רבי זירא's concern.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The Torah's special stoning rule for an ארוסה already shows that a נשואה is not stoned, so the feared mistake could never happen.

steps.title: Maybe striking a parent was the worry
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי tries a second candidate. Perhaps רבי זירא was worried about מכה אביו ואמו, whose פסוק also says ״מות יומת״, being learned from אוב וידעוני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, perhaps the case of one who strikes his father or mother troubled him, that we would come and learn it from אוב וידעוני?
steps.whatsHappening: After the first suggestion failed, רב אחא מדפתי tests a new one: the person who strikes a parent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מכה אביו ואמו is another case where the תורה says ״מות יומת״ without telling us which death. If the link to אוב וידעוני came from ״מות יומתו״, this person might wrongly get סקילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a new suggestion after the first one failed)
One who strikes and wounds his father or mother

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶלָּא, מַכֵּה אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rather, one who strikes his father or mother was troubling him,
phrases.notes: שמות 21:15

phrases.english: that we would come and learn it from אוב and ידעוני?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא, מַכֵּה אָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 11 rejected אשת איש, offers a second candidate for רבי זירא's concern.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was מכה אביו ואמו the case that made רבי זירא afraid of linking through ״מות יומתו״?

steps.title: Striking a parent would be compared to the married woman instead
steps.stepSummary: This suggestion is rejected too. Rather than comparing the striker to אוב וידעוני, we would compare him to אשת איש, because an unspecified death penalty is read the lenient way. So he would not get סקילה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before they learn from אוב וידעוני, let them learn from a married woman, since you may not stretch an unspecified death penalty to make it stricter, only to make it more lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדפתי rejects the second suggestion. Neither case explains what troubled רבי זירא, so in the next step רבינא gives the real answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אשת איש and מכה אביו ואמו have a plain ״מות יומת״ with no details. There is a rule that such an open-ended death penalty must be read leniently, not strictly. So the striker would be compared to אשת איש, who we just saw is not stoned, and never to the stricter סקילה of אוב וידעוני.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather than learning (before you learn it from there)
To be strict (here, to give a harsher death)
To be lenient (here, to give a lighter death)
Permitted, allowed

steps.confusionAlert: Being 'lenient' here does not mean the person goes free. He still gets the death penalty; the question is only which kind, and we choose the lighter one rather than סקילה.

phrases.english: Rather than learning it from אוב and ידעוני,
let them learn it from a married woman,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי אַתָּה רַשַּׁאי לְמוֹשְׁכָהּ לְהַחְמִיר עָלֶיהָ,
phrases.english: since you are not allowed to pull it toward being strict,
phrases.notes: 'It' is a death penalty the תורה states without saying which kind, like these ״מות יומת״ cases.

phrases.english: but only toward being lenient.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד דְּגָמְרִי מֵאוֹב וְיִדְּעוֹנִי, לִיגְמְרוּ מֵאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the מכה אביו ואמו suggestion from step 12 by relying on the result of step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects מכה אביו ואמו as the source of רבי זירא's concern. רבינא answers רב אחא מדפתי's question in the next step.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An unspecified death penalty is learned toward leniency, so the striker would be compared to אשת איש, who is not stoned, and not to אוב וידעוני.

steps.title: רבינא explains what really bothered רבי זירא
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers רב אחא מדפתי. The problem was not אשת איש or מכה אביו ואמו. The problem was the rest of the נסקלין themselves. If their punishment came from ״מות יומת״, they could be learned from אשת איש, and then they would get חנק instead of סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is the rest of those who are stoned themselves that bothered him. If we learned them from ״מות יומת״, then instead of learning from אוב וידעוני, we could learn from אשת איש!
steps.whatsHappening: After two suggestions were rejected, רבינא gives the real answer to why רבי זירא made sure the link came from ״דמיהם בם״ and not from ״מות יומת״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״מות יומת״ appear by אוב וידעוני, which gets סקילה, and also by אשת איש, which gets חנק. If the other sinners were linked through ״מות יומת״, we would have two possible sources, and the rule is to choose the lighter one. They would end up with חנק, which is wrong, so the link must come from ״דמיהם בם״.

keyTerms.meaning: The rest of the people who are executed by stoning
Themselves; the very cases being discussed
They learn (one case from another through a shared word)
Let them learn instead

steps.whatToRemember: The punishment of סקילה for the other sinners is learned from ״דמיהם בם״, not from ״מות יומת״. ״מות יומת״ could also point to אשת איש, and her death is the lighter חנק.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבינא answering רב אחא מדפתי's question from earlier.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁאָר הַנִּסְקָלִין גּוּפַיְיהוּ קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: It is the rest of those who are stoned themselves that bothered him,
because if they learn from "they shall be put to death,"
then rather than learning from the necromancer and the sorcerer,
let them learn from a married woman!
phrases.notes: Her punishment is the lighter חנק, so learning from her would take away their סקילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שְׁאָר הַנִּסְקָלִין גּוּפַיְיהוּ קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both suggested worries (אשת איש in step 10 and מכה אביו ואמו in step 12) were rejected, this gives the real answer to the question asked in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did רבי זירא object to the link coming from ״מות יומת״?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because then the rest of the נסקלין could be learned from אשת איש and would get only חנק. So the link must come from ״דמיהם בם״.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: סקילה for the other sinners comes from the shared words ״דמיהם בם״ with אוב וידעוני.

steps.title: The משנה lists those who are executed by stoning
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins with a list of everyone who gets סקילה. It starts with forbidden relationships, then lists sins against ה׳, then other sins, and ends with the בן סורר ומורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These are the ones who are stoned: one who sins with his mother, with his father's wife, with his daughter-in-law, with a male, with an animal, and a woman who brings an animal onto herself. Also one who curses ה׳, one who worships idols, one who gives his child to מולך, the בעל אוב and the ידעוני, one who breaks שבת, one who curses his father or mother, one who sins with a betrothed נערה, the מסית, the מדיח, the מכשף, and the בן סורר ומורה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with the full list of the sinners who are put to death by סקילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list is the table of contents for the rest of the פרק. The משנה will now go through the items one by one, starting with the relationship sins.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, meaning 'our משנה'
One who curses ה׳'s Name (blasphemer)
An idol worshipped by handing over one's children to it
One who pushes individuals toward idol worship / one who pushes a whole city toward it
The stubborn and rebellious son

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
These are the ones who are stoned:

phrases.aramaic: הַבָּא עַל הָאֵם, וְעַל אֵשֶׁת הָאָב,
phrases.english: One who has relations with his mother, or with his father's wife,
or with his daughter-in-law, or with a male,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל הַבְּהֵמָה, וְהָאִשָּׁה הַמְּבִיאָה אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה.
phrases.english: or with an animal, and a woman who brings an animal onto herself.
And one who curses ה׳, and one who worships idols,
and one who gives of his children to Molekh,
and a necromancer and a sorcerer,
and one who desecrates Shabbat,
and one who curses his father or his mother,
and one who has relations with a betrothed young woman,
and the inciter, and the one who leads a city astray,
and the warlock, and the stubborn and rebellious son.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ הֵן הַנִּסְקָלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fixed list of eighteen kinds of sinners are executed by סקילה.

steps.title: One who sins with his mother: two prohibitions or one
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts explaining its list. One who sins with his mother, who is also his father's wife, is liable for two prohibitions: אם and אשת אב. רבי יהודה says he is liable only for אם.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who has relations with his mother is liable for her because of 'mother' and because of 'father's wife'. רבי יהודה says: He is liable only because of 'mother'.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the first item on the list and brings a מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His mother is usually also his father's wife, so one act breaks two different איסורים. The תנא קמא counts both. רבי יהודה counts only the איסור of אם. Since he gets סקילה either way, the difference matters for someone who did it by accident and must bring a חטאת for each איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable; held responsible
Because of; on account of (a specific prohibition)
Father's wife
Only

phrases.english: One who has relations with his mother

phrases.aramaic: חַיָּיב עָלֶיהָ מִשּׁוּם אֵם וּמִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אָב.
phrases.english: is liable for her because of 'mother' and because of 'father's wife.'
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם הָאֵם בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: He is liable only because of 'mother' alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבָּא עַל הָאֵם, חַיָּיב עָלֶיהָ מִשּׁוּם אֵם וּמִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the first item in the list from step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: liable for both אם and אשת אב. רבי יהודה: liable only for אם.

steps.title: One who sins with his father's wife
steps.stepSummary: One who sins with his father's wife is liable for two prohibitions, אשת אב and אשת איש. The איסור of אשת אב applies while the father is alive and after he dies, and whether she was only betrothed or fully married to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who has relations with his father's wife is liable because of 'father's wife' and because of 'married woman', whether during his father's lifetime or after his father's death, whether from betrothal or from marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the second item on the list, the father's wife, and shows how far this איסור reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the father is alive and married to her, she is both his father's wife and a married woman, so two איסורים apply. The איסור of אשת אב goes further. It stays even after the father dies, and it applies even if the father had only done אירוסין.

keyTerms.meaning: A married woman
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
Full marriage, the second stage
His father's death

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'whether in his father's lifetime or after his death' goes on the איסור of אשת אב. After the father dies she is no longer an אשת איש from him, but she is still forbidden as his father's wife.

phrases.english: One who has relations with his father's wife

phrases.aramaic: חַיָּיב מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אָב וּמִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ,
phrases.english: is liable because of 'father's wife' and because of 'married woman,'
whether during his father's lifetime
or after his father's death,
whether she was his father's wife through betrothal
or through full marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבָּא עַל אֵשֶׁת אָב, חַיָּיב מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אָב וּמִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the list, moving from the mother to the father's wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relations with a father's wife bring liability for אשת אב and for אשת איש. The איסור of אשת אב applies even after the father's death and even after only אירוסין.

steps.title: One who sins with his daughter-in-law
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that one who sins with his כלה is liable for two prohibitions, כלתו and אשת איש. The כלה prohibition applies during the son's life and after his death, and whether she was only betrothed or fully married to the son.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who has relations with his daughter-in-law is liable for her because of 'his daughter-in-law' and because of 'a married woman.' This is true both during his son's lifetime and after his son's death, both from betrothal and from marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives one more case in its list: a man who sins with his son's wife. It follows the same pattern as the אשת אב case in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the son is alive, she is both his כלה and a married woman, so there are two prohibitions. The כלה prohibition is permanent: it stays after the son dies, and it starts as soon as she is betrothed to the son. Only the אשת איש part depends on the son being alive and married to her.

keyTerms.meaning: His daughter-in-law (his son's wife)
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
Full marriage, the second stage

phrases.english: One who has relations with his daughter-in-law,
is liable for her because of 'his daughter-in-law'
and because of 'a married woman,'
whether during his son's lifetime
phrases.notes: This part is about the כלה prohibition only; the אשת איש part needs the son to be alive.

phrases.english: or after his son's death,
whether from betrothal
or from full marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבָּא עַל כַּלָּתוֹ, חַיָּיב עָלֶיהָ מִשּׁוּם כַּלָּתוֹ וּמִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's explanation with a parallel case to אשת אב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who sins with his כלה is liable for both כלתו and אשת איש. The כלה prohibition applies during and after the son's life, from betrothal or marriage.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: liable only for mother if she was not fit for the father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא explaining רבי יהודה's view from the משנה. If the mother was not fit to be married to the father, the son is liable only for אם and not for אשת אב.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says, if his mother was not fit for his father, he is liable only because of 'mother.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and goes back to רבי יהודה's view about a man who sins with his mother (step 16). A ברייתא tells us when exactly רבי יהודה says there is only one prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה just said 'only for אם' without explaining. The ברייתא adds the condition: this is when the mother was not fit to marry the father. Then she does not count as the father's wife, so the אשת אב prohibition does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Fit (allowed) to be married to his father
Only

phrases.english: גמרא
It was taught: רבי יהודה says,

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא הָיְתָה אִמּוֹ רְאוּיָה לְאָבִיו,
phrases.english: if his mother was not fit for his father,
he is liable only
because of 'mother' alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יהודה's view in the משנה and explains when it applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, if the mother was not fit for the father, the son is liable only for אם.

steps.title: What does 'not fit for him' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of relationship counts as 'not fit' in רבי יהודה's words.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'she is not fit for him' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'not fit' means here. This sets up the next step, where it will try one answer and reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are different levels of forbidden relationships: some carry כרת or a death penalty, and some are only a לאו. The גמרא wants to know which level רבי יהודה is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: What? What does it mean?

phrases.english: What does 'she is not fit for him' mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״אֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the key term in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of forbidden relationship makes the mother 'not fit' for the father.

steps.title: It cannot mean a כרת or death-penalty relationship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests 'not fit' means a relationship punished by כרת or מיתת בית דין, but rejects it. Then the חכמים would hold the son is still liable for אשת אב, which makes no sense, because קידושין never take effect in such a relationship.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means those liable for כרת and those liable for court death penalties, that would imply that the חכמים hold he is liable even though she is not fit for him. But he has no קידושין with her at all!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one explanation and shows that it creates a problem. If רבי יהודה meant כרת cases, the חכמים would have to disagree, and that is impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the חכמים argue with רבי יהודה, whatever case he means must be one where they hold she is still the father's wife. But everyone agrees that קידושין do not work at all in a כרת or death-penalty relationship. So no one could say she is the father's wife there, and this cannot be the case they argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion the גמרא will reject)
Relationships punished by כרת
Relationships punished by a court death penalty
By inference, this implies
Betrothal, the act that makes a woman a man's wife

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about רבי יהודה's own view. It is about what the חכמים would have to hold if this were the case, and that is what makes it impossible.

phrases.english: If you say: those liable for כרת
and those liable for court death penalties,
that would imply that the חכמים hold

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לוֹ?
phrases.english: that he is liable even though she is not fit for him?
phrases.notes: 'Liable' means liable for אשת אב too, since the חכמים disagree with רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: But he has no קידושין with her!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא חַיָּיבֵי כָרֵיתוֹת וְחַיָּיבֵי מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין, מִכְּלָל דְּרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question and immediately attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that 'not fit' means a כרת or death-penalty relationship.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Then the חכמים would hold she is the father's wife there, but everyone agrees קידושין do not take effect in such relationships.

steps.title: It means a relationship forbidden by a לאו, following רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'not fit' means a relationship forbidden only by a לאו. רבי יהודה follows רבי עקיבא, who says קידושין do not take effect there, so she is not the father's wife. The חכמים hold they do take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means those liable for a לאו, and רבי יהודה holds like רבי עקיבא, who said: קידושין do not take effect with those liable for a לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning of 'not fit': a marriage forbidden only by a regular prohibition (a לאו). This settles what רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a לאו relationship there is a real argument about whether קידושין work. רבי יהודה sides with רבי עקיבא that they do not, so the mother never became the father's wife and there is no אשת אב. The חכמים hold the קידושין work, so the son is liable for both אם and אשת אב.

keyTerms.meaning: Relationships forbidden by a regular negative commandment (a לאו), without כרת or death
Take effect, 'take hold'
The תנא who holds קידושין do not work in a לאו relationship

steps.whatToRemember: 'Not fit' means a לאו relationship. רבי יהודה, like רבי עקיבא, holds the marriage never took effect, so the son is liable only for אם. The חכמים hold it did, so he is liable for אם and אשת אב.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the argument in the משנה about the mother is really an argument about whether קידושין take effect in a לאו relationship.

phrases.english: Rather: those liable for a לאו,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: and רבי יהודה holds like רבי עקיבא,
who said: קידושין do not take effect
with those liable for a לאו.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: חַיָּיבֵי לָאוִין, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected suggestion with the correct definition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not fit' might mean a כרת or death-penalty relationship.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Not fit' means a לאו relationship. רבי יהודה follows רבי עקיבא that קידושין do not take effect there, while the חכמים hold they do.

steps.title: רב אושעיא challenges from the משנה about איסור מצוה and איסור קדושה
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא quotes a משנה: a יבמה forbidden to the יבם by an איסור מצוה or an איסור קדושה does חליצה but not יבום. He uses this to challenge the explanation in step 22.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא raised an objection: A woman forbidden by an איסור מצוה or an איסור קדושה does חליצה and does not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא quotes a משנה to challenge the explanation just given for רבי יהודה's view. This line sets up the objection; the גמרא will spell out the exact problem in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An איסור קדושה is a prohibition carried by a לאו, such as a widow and a כהן גדול. Here the יבם himself is forbidden to her by that לאו, yet the משנה says she still needs חליצה, so the bond of יבום with him takes hold. That seems to clash with רבי עקיבא's view from step 22: if קידושין cannot take effect between them, she should be fully exempt, as with an ערוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection, usually from a משנה or ברייתא
A prohibition from a rule of the Sages, such as relatives of the second degree
A prohibition tied to the holiness of כהונה, such as a widow and a כהן גדול
The ceremony that releases a widow from the bond of יבום
Levirate marriage, when the dead husband's brother marries the widow

steps.confusionAlert: Doing חליצה does not mean she is allowed to do יבום. The prohibition blocks יבום, but the bond still exists, so חליצה is needed to release her.

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya raises an objection:
A prohibition of מצוה and a prohibition of sanctity:
phrases.notes: This is quoted from a משנה in יבמות. There, איסור קדושה means cases like a widow and a כהן גדול, which are forbidden by a לאו.

phrases.english: they perform halitza and do not enter levirate marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of step 22 that 'not fit' means a relationship forbidden by a לאו, explained through רבי עקיבא's view
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that רבי יהודה's 'not fit' means a relationship forbidden only by a לאו, following רבי עקיבא that קידושין do not take effect there
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires חליצה for a יבמה forbidden to her יבם by an איסור קדושה, which is a לאו. This treats the bond of יבום with a forbidden יבם as real, which seems to clash with רבי עקיבא's view that קידושין do not take effect in relationships forbidden by a לאו. The full point of the attack follows in the next lines.
